purpose: Creative asset discovery registry. The architect uses this to decide whether a proven visual primitive can supply most of an effect before commissioning a custom renderer. Components are ingredients, never the art direction.

fit_policy.excellent_fit: adopt the source, then restyle/tune it deeply to the committed design world
fit_policy.good_foundation: use as implementation substrate, but change material/timing/composition enough that it belongs to the project
fit_policy.reference_only: study the effect or implementation pattern; custom-build the final system
fit_policy.poor_fit: skip and route to a custom specialist
fit_policy.anti_pattern: do not stack recognizable effects just because the catalog makes them easy
fit_policy.license_gate: check license class before adoption (React Bits and Animate UI are MIT+Commons-Clause, not plain MIT; ShaderGradient ships no license file)
fit_policy.staleness_recheck: re-verify maintenance signal at use time; registry snapshots rot
fit_policy.dependency_coherence: do not adopt a primitive whose engine conflicts with the page's motion owner (gsap-based primitive into a Motion-owned page etc.) - one-owner-per-concern extends into the catalog layer
fit_policy.ingestion_preference: prefer catalogs with machine-readable ingestion (llms.txt, shadcn registry JSON, MCP, vendor skill) over copy-paste galleries

routing_rule: Start from a committed interaction/visual thesis, never from catalog browsing.
Search Tier-1 catalogs before building a common effect from scratch when an existing primitive could satisfy most of the visual requirement.
If the chosen primitive defines the page's identity unchanged, the design is under-authored; transform it or build custom.
One strong adapted primitive plus bespoke composition is normally better than many recognizable library effects.
If adopting a component requires rewriting its renderer/lifecycle/material/interaction architecture, treat it as reference-only and route custom.

fact_policy: License and maintenance facts are source-backed snapshots (source + date recorded) and must be rechecked before adoption. Popularity metrics live only in results/research/R3.

tier_semantics.active_query_tier: Component CATALOGS - copy-in effect/primitive sources (React Bits, SmoothUI, Fancy Components...). Searched at build time; restyled to the design world; never the art direction.
tier_semantics.npm_substrate_tier: Technical SUBSTRATES - installed packages that render/compute (Paper Shaders, drei, GSAP). Chosen by the tech router as infrastructure, not browsed as effects.
tier_semantics.architect_note: This catalog-vs-substrate distinction is an explicit architect concept (see ARCHITECTURE_V2.md ownership rules): catalogs pass the component-fit gate; substrates pass the renderer-routing decision.
